title: The whole icon workflow runs start to finish in one walk at Next defaults
goal: Every step of making an icon has been proved on its own, but nothing has yet gone from an empty window to a moving SVG in one go, and the focus says it must be walked end to end. Doing it once, the way a person would, shows what still trips someone up between the steps.
notes: Found in the digest of 2026-11-07. The focus in queue/objectives.json names the workflow: start a 24 unit icon, keylines and snapping on, draw a cloud-download glyph from shapes and the Pen, union it, give it a 1.75 round stroke, check it at 16, 24 and 48, make it swing or spin forever, export an animated SVG for a web page. No walk under Scripts/playtest does more than a part of this (grep for cloud finds only opening-an-svg-walk and border-follows-the-shape-walk). Stepping along the first half by hand found the typed Width fault at once, so expect more. While walking, judge the panel too: a rectangle in an icon frame shows Columns and Layout sections that say little about an icon (queue/audits/2026-11-07-icon-place-tag-1-box-sc.png, and the same on 2026-11-06). Seen twice now. If it gets in the way, say so in the audit. Each fault this finds that is not a one line fix gets its own task; do not fold them all in here.
acceptance: One walk at Next defaults with no flags does every step of the focus workflow, on File, New, Image, Icon and again on a 24 unit frame, through pointer clicks and keys, and exports an animated SVG
The exported SVG is opened in a browser and plays, and the audit says so with a picture
The audit lists every step that was clumsy, surprising or took a second try, as a person trying it would see them, with a picture for each
Any step that fails either passes before this closes or has its own open task named in the audit

log.note: Before building: walked the flow as a first-time user. The stops I expected were where to find Join, how to swing a whole glyph when Add Key takes one layer, and how a loop gets home. All three turned out to be real.

Chose fixing the crop, the straight line and its tile in the shared renderer over a Next flag, because they are plain drawing bugs and a flag would keep a wrong picture on purpose; Current gets the same correct pixels.
Chose to keep the walks on front:true, because SwiftUI takes these clicks only in the app in front and it gives pictures in the real colours; they wait for the Mac like the 27 others.
Browser proof: real time headless Chrome over its debugging port and a WKWebView, reading the live angle of the animated group. Virtual time was tried first and read nothing, so it is not used.

left rough: a part's tile in a 24 point frame is blurry because tiles never upscale; two snapping rows in View (Snap to Grid is dimmed on an Icon picture, Snap in Icons is live); Applies to 1 of the 3 selected layers shows under Fill when three lines are picked. None stopped the walk.

Two walks at Next defaults go from an empty window to an animated SVG, on File, New, Image, Icon and on a 24 unit frame (the-whole-icon-workflow-walk, -on-a-frame-walk). Both files play and loop in real time Chrome and WebKit, with live angles read and a contact sheet in the audit. Fixed three faults it found: a turned group cropping thick lines at 2x, a straight line drawn soft with an empty tile, the Export sheet saying a looping icon stops. Filed a-playing-icon-stays-sharp-on-a-zoomed-canvas, a-looping-turn-comes-home-and-spins-evenly-witho, a-group-in-an-icon-shows-what-an-icon-needs-not; folded the Pen mismatch into a-glyph-takes-the-icon-set-s-saved-stroke-in-one. Scripts/test.sh exit 0. The save panel itself was not driven: the walk opens the real sheet and writes the file with writeSVG.
